results.title: heal.dev: Find bugs and vulnerabilities code review misses | Product Hunt
results.content:
The key difference

👉 Review bots find what a developer would change to keep code clean. A lot of findings.

👉 Heal finds a proven user behaviour that causes a bug. Fewer findings, closer to the user.

With Heal, you get high-signal, verified bugs and vulnerabilities users would see, and a completely autonomous system. It's free during the beta, no cc required: www.heal.dev

Debate club 🥊 Ding ding ding!

One question for y'all: what makes it so that you don't auto-merge all PRs? Could Heal be the reason you finally do?

Georges Biaux

@therealmalo 💪🏻

Amaury Soviche [...] Yvan Derogis

I've tested heal.dev heavily (disclaimer: Malo is a friend!) and other solutions/competitors, and this new version of heal is far far better than the inifinite-and-never-ending-list-of-vibe-coded-in-30-days E2E tools that I've also tested. heal creates a flywheel/loop where you can let Claude/Codex code an app, then give it to heal that finds vulnerabilities/bugs missed by Claude/Codex, then let Claude/Codex repair that, and then verify Claude/Codex work with heal, so for some parts of tools I work on, the result after this automatic loop is excellent and much better than Claude/Codex alone.

Malo Marrec

Thank you@yvan\_derogis  and thanks for the harsh feedback when we needed harsh feedback!

Florian Bienefelt [...] Florian Bienefelt

Been using heal.dev to poke holes into our software and it's been really awesome to get these complete, reproducible, lists of issues that I can then throw tokens at to solve.  
  
I think these kinds of grindy agent loops will make codebases converge towards perfection if you apply it to all sorts of gardening in a codebase, like security, patching, refinement, uniformity in design, test flakes, codebase health, etc.

Malo Marrec

Thanks @florian\_bienefelt !

Raphael Moutard

We tried after many code review tools. it's not juste code review Heal found things we didn't expect, that would have costs us $1000 in pen test!

Malo Marrec

Thanks @raphael\_moutard1 !
